exercise.name: Deep Push-Up

reference.title: Deep Push-Up
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

equipment: Two low boxes or push-up blocks

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you sink between the blocks, exhale as you press up.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, short pause, about 1.2 s up

prescription.progression: Deeper blocks, slower lowering, then a weighted vest

cues.text: Hands on two low blocks well outside the shoulders, arms straight, body in one line on the balls of the feet.
Breathe in and lower the chest between the blocks, elbows back at about 45 degrees.
Sink until the chest is below the hands: a stretch across the chest, shoulders still down.
Breathe out and press up through the palms.
Arms straight at the top; reset and go again.

mistakes.fix: Lower under control and stop where the shoulders still feel strong.

mistakes.mistake: Shoulders rolling forward at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest open and the shoulder blades drawn back.
Brace the abs and squeeze the glutes.

mistakes.mistake: Blocks too far apart or wobbly
mistakes.fix: Use stable blocks just outside shoulder width.

kinematics.norm: Wide (well outside the shoulders), palms on raised blocks so the chest can travel below hand level (clinical opinion)
Arms straight but not locked at the top; elbows bend to about 90 degrees or more at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Elbow tuck (upper arm from the trunk)
kinematics.norm: Elbows close to the ribs, about 10-30 degrees from the body at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Head, trunk, hips and ankles (or knees) in one straight line throughout (clinical opinion)
Palms flat; the wrist bends back about 80-90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1 s up; lab studies used 2-2.5 s per repetition (Marcolin 2015)
Chest a few centimetres below the top of the blocks at the bottom; more range than a floor push-up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Marcolin, Petrone, Moro, Battaglia, Bianco and Paoli 2015, selective activation of shoulder, trunk and arm muscles: a comparative analysis of different push-up variants (J Athl Train 50(11):1126-1132)
Kim, Kim and Ha 2016, effect of the push-up exercise at different palmar width on muscle activities (J Phys Ther Sci 28(2):446-449; PMC4792988)

cautions: Shoulder pain: the extra depth stretches the front of the shoulder; reduce the depth if the front of the shoulder aches (clinical opinion).
Use stable blocks that cannot slide or tip.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: lower blocks or stop at hand level.
Too hard: knees down on the mat.
progressions: Slow 3 s lowering with a pause.
